(b) optimize=2 also hides  statements, the one construct that compare could mask, so I counted them separately via ast.walk: 0 asserts in both revisions, identical. (c) POSITIONAL: parsed both and took repo_revision's docstring node span -- pre (575,614), post (575,615) -- then took every changed line number from 'git diff -U0': pre side 587-599, post side 587-600. EVERY changed line on BOTH sides lies strictly inside that docstring's own span. Nothing outside repo_revision moved; the file grew by exactly one line. c3-guard-depth.title: CLAIM 3: regression guard is depth-complete + encoded-token fragility
c3-guard-depth.imperative: Assess test_dirty_appears_nowhere_in_the_manifest for depth-completeness and decide whether the assertNotIn('dirty', cm.encode(m)) token check is fragile enough to be a finding. Red-prove the guard against the SHIPPED blob with a mutation OUTSIDE the spent set; record the blob OID and assert the SPECIFIC named assertion, never a non-zero exit. Restore in finally:.
c3-guard-depth.finding: CLAIM 3 CONFIRMED, and the fragility question RULED as an observation + followup, NOT a blocker. FOUR mutations, all NEW (outside the g1-g3 spent set), all applied to the SHIPPED worktree file scripts/context_manifest.py at blob 6ea9dccbab245c8d549a832cb6792cd18ff84d3c (#381 satisfied: proved against what ships, not against a revision), all confirmed by blob-OID CHANGE, all restored in a finally: with blob-OID MATCH back to 6ea9dcc, and each adjudicated by the SPECIFIC named assertion in the pytest source line, never by exit code. M0-field-returns-to-run (wrap the run subtree so dirty is merged back in; mutated OID a3a460e9a98ad0d486d1702df6ab95d6955292b8): first failure is the source line self.assertNotIn('dirty', m['run']). M1-nested-under-run-host (inject dirty at depth 3, inside run.host, where ALL THREE flat assertNotIn checks are structurally blind; mutated OID 41f9a7237fa5fc53a2fcf6789d673db1a0b922ef): first failure is self.assertEqual(_dirty_key_paths(m), []) with 'Lists differ: [/run/host/dirty] != []'. M2-nested-inside-a-files-list-row (inject dirty into a row dict inside the files LIST, exercising the sweep's list-recursion branch; mutated OID 35ae21565bf1351bd300bdd6df29365336bf579e): first failure is self.assertEqual(_dirty_key_paths(m), []) with 'Lists differ: [/files/0/dirty] != []'. So depth-completeness is not a claim, it is now measured in both the dict and the list branch. M3-token-as-a-VALUE-not-a-key (set run.host.platform to the string 'dirty'; mutated OID 43c4ae38ce4cc115333cf12f186b05609e0030f6) is the decisive one for the fragility ruling: _dirty_key_paths returned [] -- the structural sweep is BLIND to it by construction, it matches keys only -- and the ONLY assertion that fired was self.assertNotIn('dirty', cm.encode(m)). The encode-token layer is therefore genuinely COMPLEMENTARY, not belt-and-braces redundancy: it covers the value-shaped re-introduction (a 'status': 'dirty' or a flag list) that the sweep provably cannot see. RULING on fragility: the check IS value-sensitive -- that is exactly what makes it useful and exactly what makes it trippable, one property, not two -- but (a) the failure direction is a false RED, loud and safe, never a false GREEN; (b) the fixture is fully controlled (work_id 'w-1' from the checklist() helper, roots under tempfile.TemporaryDirectory); (c) the implementer's own trip came from hand-choosing a work_id containing the token, which the shipped fixture does not do. Residual exposure is a developer whose TMPDIR path contains the substring 'dirty', which would spuriously red the test. Narrowing the token to the JSON key form would DESTROY the M3 coverage, so narrowing is the wrong fix. FOLLOWUP (not blocking): add one warning line to the comment above that assertion saying it matches values as well as keys, so the next author who picks a descriptive work_id does not spend the time the implementer spent. Filed as a triage candidate.

Ordering the eight manifests in .agent-work/issue-305/context by run.generated_at puts g1-review.json FIRST at 02:52:37Z with dirty=true, and g1-implement.json SECOND at 03:00:53Z. Creation order in git agrees and is independent of the timestamps inside the files: git log --diff-filter=A (no --follow, which lies through rename ancestry) shows g1-review.json created at b1707f1 and g1-implement.json created eight minutes LATER at bcb0975, whose subject is 'gate(#305): reopen g1 for the ruled packaging rework'. Widening 'the run' does not rescue it either: the earliest manifest anywhere in the corpus is .agent-work/issue-305/issue-305-g1-implement/context/m4-failsoft.json at 02:16:39Z, dirty=true, and every one of the nine context directories' earliest manifest reads true or is field-absent. (2) The CAUSE is not 'no predecessor'. The surviving file is a REOPEN artifact: its repo_rev.commit is 2456130, which landed at 19:58:37-07:00 = 02:58:37Z, two minutes sixteen seconds before the manifest was generated at 03:00:53Z, and bcb0975 committed it 51 seconds after that. The tree read clean because a commit had just cleaned it, not because nothing preceded it. So the false records a momentarily-clean tree during a gate reopen. SEPARATE OBSERVATION on the same sentence: the COUNT is sound but is stated as a live tree property with no anchor. My sweep of every .agent-work JSON carrying {contract,step,files,run} finds 56 manifests at 35d2686 and at HEAD: 51 true, 1 false, 4 field-absent -- not 49/47/1/1. It reconciles EXACTLY: the doc's 49 was measured at the start of g4-implement, and that run then wrote 4 more pre-removal manifests (all true, 47+4=51) and 3 post-removal ones (field-absent, 1+3=4), 49+7=56. The commit message anchors the measurement ('at the point of removal'); the SHIPPED DOC does not, so main will carry a number that was already stale when it was written.
